work_types.name: Concrete pouring
work_types.reference_note: Fresh concrete hydration requires temperatures above 5 C to avoid ice damage to the paste and below 30 C to limit rapid moisture loss and thermal cracking; surface water intrusion during placement compromises the water-cement ratio.

work_types.name: Concrete surface finishing
work_types.reference_note: Surface finishing operations require the same temperature band as placement; wind above 10 m/s accelerates surface moisture loss faster than bleed water can replace it, causing plastic shrinkage cracking.

work_types.name: Floor screed pouring
work_types.reference_note: Screed layers are thinner than structural pours and lose surface moisture faster, so the wind limit is tighter than concrete_pour; the temperature and curing requirements otherwise mirror general cementitious placement.

work_types.name: Masonry laying
work_types.reference_note: Mortar bedding needs above 5 C to cure without frost damage; masonry units have lower thermal mass than a concrete pour, so the upper temperature limit is relaxed to 35 C.

work_types.name: Exterior painting
work_types.reference_note: Solvent evaporation and film formation degrade below 10 C and above 80% relative humidity.

work_types.name: Facade plastering
work_types.reference_note: Plaster set and adhesion fail below 5 C, and wind above 10 m/s combined with humidity above 85% causes uneven surface drying and shrinkage cracking on the facade.

work_types.name: Waterproofing coating
work_types.reference_note: Waterproofing coatings require a dry, stable substrate; wind above 8 m/s and humidity above 80% prevent proper film curing and risk trapping moisture beneath the membrane.

work_types.name: Roofing membrane installation
work_types.reference_note: Membrane seams rely on adhesive or heat-welded bonds that fail to set below 5 C; wind above 10 m/s makes handling large membrane sheets on an elevated roof unsafe.

work_types.name: Bitumen roofing application
work_types.reference_note: Hot bitumen application involves open flame or molten material; the tighter wind limit reflects both flame stability and the safety risk of handling hot material at height in gusty conditions.

work_types.name: Structural steel welding
work_types.reference_note: Welding generates its own heat and tolerates low ambient temperature, but wind above 12 m/s disperses shielding gas and destabilizes the arc, degrading weld quality.

work_types.name: Asphalt paving
work_types.reference_note: Asphalt must be compacted before it cools below its workable temperature; ambient temperatures below 10 C cause the mat to lose heat too quickly for proper compaction.

work_types.name: Excavation
work_types.reference_note: Earthmoving equipment operates across a wide temperature and humidity range; precipitation is permitted since it does not by itself halt excavation, though the illustrative thresholds do not model soil saturation or slope stability effects.
